title: Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
abstract: arXiv:2608.20231v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The standard objection to full automation is demand-side: if humans earn nothing, who buys the output? This confuses an accounting role with a biological species. We model a post-AGI economy in which corporations own populations of AI and robotic agents that are both producers and consumers of energy, compute, maintenance, and upgrades, traded among firms. Three results follow. (i) Demand closure: a closed inter-corporate economy with zero human consumption is not degenerate; it is the classical von Neumann expanding economy, whose growth rate is well defined, positive, and maximal precisely because all output is reinvested. (ii) Bottleneck removal: once economic agents are manufactured rather than reared, the binding constraint on growth shifts from human demography (a ~20-year, non-parallelizable reproduction technology capped at a few percent per year) to fabrication throughput and energy capture, permitting growth one to two orders

translated_title: 无人类增长：机器消费者、企业循环性与AGI后GDP与人类脱钩
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20231v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：对完全自动化的标准反对意见来自需求侧：如果人类不赚取任何收入，谁购买产出？这混淆了会计角色与生物物种。我们建模了一个后AGI经济，其中公司拥有AI和机器人代理群体，这些代理既是生产者又是能源、计算、维护和升级的消费者，并在企业间交易。三个结果随之而来。（i）需求闭合：一个零人类消费的封闭企业间经济并非退化；它是经典的冯·诺依曼扩张经济，其增长率定义明确、为正且最大，正因为所有产出都被再投资。（ii）瓶颈消除：一旦经济代理被制造而非抚养，增长的约束条件从人类人口统计学（一种约20年、不可并行化的繁殖技术，年增长率上限为几个百分点）转向制造吞吐量和能源捕获，允许增长率提高一到两个数量级。
tldr: 本文提出后AGI经济中，企业拥有的AI和机器人代理构成闭环生产-消费系统，可脱离人类需求实现正增长，并将增长瓶颈从人口限制转向制造和能源，实现GDP与人类脱钩。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that in a post-AGI economy, corporate-owned AI and robotic agents form a closed production-consumption system, enabling positive growth independent of human demand and shifting growth bottlenecks from demographics to manufacturing and energy, decoupling GDP from humanity.
